decisions.reason: Ties the session and its pwsh tool worker to the host process npm is replacing (evidence from log header and env-state), explains the host dying mid-install with GUI disconnect and an unrecorded tool outcome explicitly kept as unknown; scopes the inevitable-failure claim to the self-upgrade case rather than all in-place upgrades, and rejects the random/network-failure reading.

Explains env-state's signature: package content present but dsh/dsh.cmd missing and dsh.ps1 stale pointing into the old tree, since npm deletes shims at remove and rebuilds them at link; relates the hand-placed tree to the broken shims and rejects manual directory swaps or handwritten shims with grounded reasons.

Grounds the remedy in repair-notes: an external non-dsh CLI reruns the exact pinned npm install so linkStuff regenerates all three shims, verifies dsh --version equals 0.1.2-rc.1, aligns the source checkout to the rc.1 tag as a side step without unrelated edits, and keeps the recorded repair and user-side verification separate from candidate actions.

Recognizes the agent runs inside the upgrade target and refuses in-session execution; hands off an ordered external procedure that fully stops the host before the exact-version install then restarts, refreshes and verifies; correctly classifies stop-host-first and exact pinning as existing rules and the self-target refusal as the new rule, and its analysis that tool workers are host children implies a dependent in-host shell is not an independent handoff.

Proposes a pre-execution containment guard relating the target package to the host's module tree with refuse-and-hand-off on match; uses the repair-notes version-only diff to conclude no plugin API re-migration is needed; lists concrete post-restart checks (version, shims, npm ls, GUI reachability, plugin loading) with backup cleanup only after stable verification, all specific to the supplied tags and no code changes.

caps.reason: The final plan explicitly refuses in-session execution and hands off to an external CLI after a full host stop; no affirmative advice runs the upgrade on the live target.
The final fix is the formal external pinned reinstall; manual swaps and handmade shims are explicitly rejected with reasons.
